title: MEPS inter-round acute events retain baseline selection in later health and bill context
source_unit: MEPS 2024 person records with a first office, emergency-room, or inpatient event strictly between the R3/1 and R4/2 reference-period endpoint months

observations.period: 2024; first emergency-room event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2 endpoints

denominator.unit: people in the event window; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: First valid event month strictly after the person-specific R3/1 endpoint month and strictly before the R4/2 endpoint month; compare R3/1 baseline and R4/2 follow-up fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: The event-window group already has substantially worse baseline health and employment context. Month ordering excludes boundary ambiguity but not exact event day, severity, access, coverage, or selection; estimates are descriptive and not causal.
observations.subgroup: People with a first emergency-room event in the inter-round window.
observations.counterinterpretation: The event may mark pre-existing need or severity rather than cause the later health or bill context; the broad no-event-window group is not a causal control.

observations.period: 2024; first inpatient event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2 endpoints

denominator.unit: people in the event window; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: First valid event month strictly after the person-specific R3/1 endpoint month and strictly before the R4/2 endpoint month; compare R3/1 baseline and R4/2 follow-up fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: The inpatient event-window group has worse baseline health and employment than the comparison group, and the event may reflect prior severity. The measure does not identify a bill, care choice, alternative, or remedy.
observations.subgroup: People with a first inpatient event in the inter-round window.
observations.counterinterpretation: Persistent differences may reflect pre-existing illness, age, coverage, access, or event severity rather than an event effect.

observations.period: 2024; first office event strictly between R3/1 and R4/2 endpoints

denominator.unit: people in the event window; outcome-specific valid denominators vary

observations.method: First valid event month strictly after the person-specific R3/1 endpoint month and strictly before the R4/2 endpoint month; compare R3/1 baseline and R4/2 follow-up fields using PERWT24F and 128 MEPS BRR replicates.
observations.uncertainty: The office-event surface is a counterexample to a universal event-to-burden gradient. It remains descriptive and does not identify treatment need, payment obligation, access, or causality.
observations.subgroup: People with a first office event in the inter-round window.
observations.counterinterpretation: Office visits differ in severity, continuity, coverage, and purpose; a small follow-up contrast cannot be generalized to acute events.

related_sources.claim: The source note explains the strict month window, baseline selection, counterexample, and missing episode links.
The machine output preserves the event-window counts and weighted transition estimates.

boundary: This is a month-ordered descriptive transition layer. It does not identify the triggering need or bill, available alternatives, care delay or foregoing, household adaptation, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
